tts: It is not something that I usually do, because I really do need my sleep. However, I do find it difficult to sleep on aeroplanes.
It was a thirteen-hour flight, and I really tried to get some sleep. I put in the earplugs and I put on the eye mask. But I just cannot sleep sitting upright.
I closed my eyes, but I did not sleep at all. Not one bit. I was exhausted when we arrived.

items.q: What is the speaker describing?
o: Failing to sleep on a long flight

items.q: What did she try?
What does she say the real problem is?

tts: Norwegian people are always asking me: how do you like the dark?

You might think that everyone would stay indoors, nice and cosy, but they do not. Instead they wrap up warm and get out in the fresh air, skiing and playing in the snow, even if it is under artificial light.
November to February is full of light because it is a time of celebrations. There are lights and candles everywhere, as people decorate their houses and gardens.

In the summer we have sixty days when the sun never really sets at all. The nights are as lively as the days, with people going to the beach and to outdoor concerts to celebrate the midnight sun. The only downside is that it is a bit difficult to sleep — but then again, who wants to?
I originally come from Pakistan, where the sun sets and rises at pretty much the same time every day.

acts.title: Habits: then, now, and the trap in the middle
rule: Three structures describe habits, and two of them look almost identical while meaning entirely different things. used to + infinitive is about the past. be used to + -ing is about the present. Mixing them is the commonest single error at B2.
points: A habit or state that was true in the past and is not now. I used to sleep eight hours.
A repeated past action only. Never a state. Every summer we would drive south.
be, have, know, like, live. There used to be a shop there — never “there would be”.
Accustomed to something now. I am used to sleeping in the light.
The process of becoming accustomed. It took me a year to get used to it.
Present simple with usually, tend to, always: I tend to wake up twice.
eg: I used to sleep straight through the night.
Past habit, now finished.
Did you use to work nights?
Question — use to, without the d.
I didn’t use to enjoy Mondays.
Negative — use to, without the d.
Every summer we would drive to the coast.
Repeated past action.
There used to be a shop on that corner.
A past state; would is impossible.
She used to know the whole family.
know is a state.
I am used to sleeping in the light.
Accustomed to it now.
It took me a year to get used to the dark.
The process of becoming accustomed.
I usually have a nap at about three.
Present habit.
I tend to wake up twice, whatever time I go to bed.
Present habit, hedged.
acts.careful: “I am used to sleep eight hours” is not English. After be used to and get used to, the next word is always an -ing form or a noun, because to here is a preposition, not part of an infinitive.

write.q: Write about 180 words on how your sleep, or your mornings, or your working day has changed over the last ten years. Use used to at least twice, would at least once for a repeated action, be used to + -ing at least once, and a present habit with tend to.
plan: one thing you would do repeatedly
what you are used to now
write.model:
Ten years ago I used to sleep straight through from midnight to seven, and I genuinely did not understand people who complained about it.

Every Sunday I would sleep until eleven, and every Monday I would feel worse for it, and it took me about six years to connect those two facts.

What changed was a job with a five-thirty alarm. There used to be a version of me who could function on six hours; that person is gone and I do not expect him back.

I am now used to waking up twice a night, which sounds worse than it is. I have stopped treating it as a problem to solve, and I tend to read for twenty minutes rather than lie there being annoyed.

The one thing I have not got used to is the winter. Getting up at the crack of dawn in July is a pleasure. In January it is simply getting up in the middle of the night.
